title: Paid Summer Internships and Jobs for High Schoolers
subtitle: Summer 2027. The pay, the deadlines, and how hard each one is to get.
fromVideo: From the video: the paid programs most students miss
intro: We checked these programs on their official websites on November 4 and 5, 2026. The Boston and Smithsonian entries say what we could not confirm. If a 2027 date is not posted, we show the last date we could find. We left out anything that charges tuition.

rule.title: How to use this list
rule.body: Pick your part, then apply to more than one. Nearly every famous program is hard to get. For most students, the city programs in Part 2 are likely the best shot.
items: Better odds: a big city program or a lottery. Still no guarantee.
Competitive: about 1 in 5 to 1 in 10 get in, or the program calls itself competitive.
Long shot: about 1 in 20 or harder.
No numbers: the program does not publish them, so plan as if it is competitive.

glance.title: Next deadlines
items: Nov 30: Navy SEAP
Jan 11: Air Force Research Lab

entries.section: Part 1: Open to students in many states
entries.title: Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
entries.pay: $4,000 stipend for about 8 weeks
entries.deadline: November 30, 2026. Open now.
entries.who: Current high schoolers who finished 9th grade and will be 16 by the start. Graduating seniors can apply. US citizens, with some lab exceptions. Labs are around the country and you handle your own transportation.
entries.oddsNote: About 300 spots across 38 labs. No applicant numbers published.

entries.title: Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Scholars
entries.pay: $506.80 a week for high schoolers at most sites, based on the latest session
entries.deadline: January 11, 2027. Open now. AFRL says dates can vary by site.
entries.who: Upper-level high schoolers, 16 by the deadline, or 18 for California sites. US citizens only. Full time at an AFRL site, so check which sites have high school topics. You must be willing to relocate and arrange your own housing. Background check required.
entries.oddsNote: Mentors rank applicants on STEM experience, classes, GPA and resume. Add a recommendation letter.

entries.title: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
entries.pay: $3,000 stipend over 8 weeks at 32 hours a week
entries.deadline: Opens November 23, 2026 and closes January 24, 2027.
entries.who: Current juniors and seniors (classes of 2028 and 2027). One FAQ answer says 16 by your start date and another says 16 by June 1, so go by June 1 to be safe. No science prerequisites. Available in all 50 states, placed within a 30 to 45 minute commute. A local mentor is not guaranteed. The program's main goal is reaching students from groups underrepresented in fisheries science.
entries.oddsNote: 30 students from 256 applications in 2022, about 1 in 8.

entries.title: NIH Summer Internship Program (seniors only)
entries.pay: $2,840 a month for high school graduates on the current table, updated yearly
entries.deadline: January 26, 2027, noon ET. Letters due February 2. Open now.
entries.who: Current seniors who graduate before starting. 18 by September 30, 2027. If you are 17 on June 1, you must live within 40 miles of an NIH campus. US citizens or permanent residents. No housing provided. Proof of health insurance required.
entries.oddsNote: Researchers pick their own interns, so email the labs you want.

entries.provider: National Park Service and other public lands
entries.title: Youth Conservation Corps
entries.pay: At least minimum wage, usually 40 hours a week
entries.deadline: 2027 applications open late January or early February. Each park sets its own deadline. 2026 deadlines ran February 13 to June 16.
entries.who: Ages 15 through 18 who are permanent residents of the US. A paid outdoor summer job, not an office internship. You commute daily, except at Yellowstone.
entries.oddsNote: Each site hires on its own, so odds depend on the site near you.

entries.title: Project SEED
entries.pay: $4,000 stipend
entries.deadline: Applications February to April 2027. Exact dates not posted. 2026 closed April 6.
entries.who: Preferably current sophomores, juniors or seniors with at least one chemistry class. Family income at or below 300% of the federal poverty guidelines, with proof. You need a host site you can commute to. Find a Location shows summer 2023 sites, so confirm yours is running.
entries.oddsNote: About 371 students from 1,685 applicants in 2024, about 1 in 5.

entries.title: OSTEM Internships (seniors who will be 18)
entries.pay: Stipend based on academic level and session length. Amount not listed.
entries.who: Current seniors, for the summer right after graduation. 18 by the June 7, 2027 start, 3.0 GPA, US citizens only. You arrange your own housing. If you graduate after June 7, ask NASA first. Current juniors cannot apply.
entries.oddsNote: These internships are built for college-level students.

entries.title: AEOP High School Internships
entries.pay: A stipend for every intern. Set by site and length.
entries.deadline: Always open, but deadlines vary by listing.
entries.who: Current high schoolers. Each posting adds its own rules, including any age minimum. US citizens or permanent residents. You must be able to commute, since housing is not provided.
entries.oddsNote: The program calls its internships highly competitive.

entries.title: Senate Page Program, summer sessions
entries.pay: Paid on a $38,547 yearly salary basis, so you earn a share for your weeks. School-year housing costs $1,380 a month from pay. Ask about summer.
entries.deadline: Set by each senator's office. Sessions in June and July 2027, exact dates not posted.
entries.who: Rising juniors and seniors who are 16 or 17 on the appointment date, with a 3.0 GPA. A senator must sponsor you, and not all senators do. US citizens or permanent residents with a Social Security number.
entries.oddsNote: 30 page positions for 100 senators. Extra commuter pages may be added in summer. Count not listed.

entries.section: Part 2: Better odds, city summer jobs
entries.title: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
entries.pay: 2026: $17 an hour, 25 hours a week for 6 weeks at ages 16 to 24
entries.deadline: 2027 not posted. 2026 deadline was March 13.
entries.who: NYC youth ages 14 to 24. Ages 14 and 15 earned up to $700 on paid projects. Free to apply.
entries.oddsNote: Random lottery, with 100,000 young people served in 2025.

entries.title: Chicago Youth Works (was One Summer Chicago)
entries.pay: Paid, but the rate depends on the program and is not listed. Library spots for younger teens are volunteer.
entries.deadline: 2027 dates not posted, though the site says the application is open. Applications ran in spring 2026.
entries.who: Chicago residents ages 14 to 24. Most summer jobs are for ages 16 and up.
entries.oddsNote: The site lists about 31,100 opportunities and 53,900 applicants last year.

entries.title: Marion Barry Summer Youth Employment Program
entries.pay: 2026: $9 an hour at ages 16 to 21, $6.25 at ages 14 and 15
entries.deadline: 2027 not posted. The 2026 application has closed.
entries.who: DC residents ages 14 to 24. The pay is low for this list.
entries.oddsNote: In 2024, employers offered 26,382 slots for 13,960 eligible youth. Slots are employer maximums.

entries.title: Grow Detroit's Young Talent
entries.pay: $12.50 to $15 an hour, or a $1,500 to $2,000 stipend. Up to 120 hours.
entries.deadline: 2027 not posted. 2026 window was March 13 to May 15.
entries.who: Detroit residents ages 14 to 24, at any household income.
entries.oddsNote: Random lottery, but thousands apply and not everyone is picked.

entries.title: Career Connected Learning PHL (formerly WorkReady)
entries.pay: $1,300 to $1,500 depending on the program, school year and summer combined
entries.deadline: 2027 not posted. Summer applications open between March and April each year. 2026 window was March 19 to April 30.
entries.who: Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24, with priority for students in school.
entries.oddsNote: The city planned 8,000 summer placements in 2024. Spots are matched by fit.

entries.title: YouthWorks
entries.pay: 2026: $15 an hour
entries.deadline: January 4 to February 27, 2027.
entries.who: Baltimore City residents. The 2026 age range was 14 to 21. Program runs June 28 to July 30, 2027.
entries.oddsNote: No job is guaranteed, and applying early does not guarantee a spot.

entries.title: futureBOS Youth Jobs (SuccessLink)
entries.pay: SuccessLink jobs: $15 an hour at ages 14 to 18, up to 25 hours a week in summer, per an archived city page. Other jobs may differ.
entries.deadline: 2027 not posted. No single deadline. For 2026, the city said to check back in March. Its site was down on November 4.
entries.who: Boston youth ages 14 and up who are allowed to work. Check each listing for its rules.
entries.oddsNote: Employers hire as applications arrive, so apply early and to at least three jobs.

entries.title: Youth@Work
entries.pay: $18.47 an hour for at least 140 hours, per the county in July 2026
entries.deadline: No fixed deadline posted. Fill out the county interest form, and a job center will contact you.
entries.who: LA County residents ages 14 to 24 in an eligible group, such as low-income households, foster youth or young people with disabilities.
entries.oddsNote: The county aimed to place at least 500 youth in summer 2026 roles. You must fit an eligible group.

entries.title: Phoenix Youth R.I.S.E.
entries.pay: 2026: $15.15 an hour for 80 hours over 4 weeks
entries.deadline: 2027 not posted.
entries.who: Phoenix residents ages 16 to 24.
entries.oddsNote: First come, first served, so watch for the opening.

entries.title: Seattle Youth Employment Program
entries.pay: 2026: at least $21.30 an hour, the highest hourly rate on this list
entries.deadline: 2027 internship dates not posted. 2026 window was March 18 to May 5. The separate Learn & Earn: Pathways program closes December 16, 2026.
entries.who: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Seattle or attend Seattle public schools, with household income at or below 80% of the area median.
entries.oddsNote: No applicant numbers published.

entries.title: Not in one of these cities?
entries.lead: Many cities and counties run a program like these. Here is how to look for yours.
items: Search your city or county name plus "summer youth employment".
Use the American Job Center Finder, then call your nearest center and ask about paid summer programs for high schoolers.
Ask your school counselor which local employers hired students last summer.
entries.note: Federal youth job funds focus on young people facing barriers to work, and at least 75% go to those out of school. Job centers can still point you to local programs.

entries.section: Part 3: Only if you live nearby
entries.title: Memorial Sloan Kettering Summer Student Program
entries.pay: $1,200 stipend, June 29 to August 20, 2027
entries.deadline: February 5, 2027, 8 a.m. EST. Opens December 1, 2026.
entries.who: Current juniors, 16 by June 2027, with a 3.5 GPA in science, living in NY, NJ or CT within 25 miles of MSK's Upper East Side campus. Must be legally authorized to work in the US.
entries.oddsNote: 20 spots, 1,000+ applications, 2% acceptance rate.

entries.title: UCSF High School Intern Program
entries.pay: $4,500 for completing 8 weeks at 35 hours a week
entries.deadline: February 15, 2027. Opens January 15.
entries.who: Current juniors at San Francisco public or charter schools. No exceptions.
entries.oddsNote: 25 spots and about 50 interviews. UCSF says acceptance does not depend on grades.

entries.title: Salk Institute High School Summer Scholars
entries.pay: Paid, 8 weeks. Amount not listed.
entries.deadline: February 15, 2027. Opens December 1, 2026.
entries.who: San Diego County residents at county high schools, 16 by June 14, 2027, with a 2.75 GPA and one biology class. Salk's 2027 flyer also lists a year of chemistry, so confirm.
entries.oddsNote: 12 students from 250 applicants in 2022, about 1 in 20.

entries.title: Fermilab PRISM
entries.pay: $500 a week for 4 weeks, July 12 to August 6, 2027
entries.deadline: March 1, 2027. Opens January 12.
entries.who: Illinois students who are rising seniors or 2027 graduates. US citizens only. One letter from a STEM teacher or club advisor. Fermilab calls this a summer school. Proof of medical insurance required.
entries.oddsNote: No course prerequisites.

entries.title: Smithsonian Natural History Summer Internship
entries.pay: Paid. We could not confirm the current amount, so check the listing.
entries.deadline: 2027 details due early December. 2026 deadline was March 20.
entries.who: Grades 9 to 12, ages 15 to 18, within commuting distance in DC, Maryland or Virginia. Check the listing for citizenship rules.
entries.oddsNote: Includes non-science museum work.

entries.title: The Met Summer High School Internship
entries.pay: 2026: $1,100 stipend for 40 hours
entries.deadline: 2027 not posted. 2026 deadline was March 13.
entries.who: Grade 10 or 11. The summer page says you must live and attend school in NY, NJ or CT, but a Met FAQ says New York City, so email them to confirm.
entries.oddsNote: Plan on heavy competition.

entries.title: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship
entries.pay: A financial award for finishing. Details go to applicants who interview.
entries.deadline: 2027 information due in November. 2026 deadline was March 13.
entries.who: Rising seniors, 16 by the start, living in Greater Seattle or nearby.
entries.oddsNote: Fred Hutch calls it highly competitive. No numbers published. Designed for students without much research experience.

entries.title: Teen Gallery Guides at the Getty
entries.pay: A stipend for finishing the program. Amount not listed.
entries.deadline: Usually opens early February. No 2027 date posted.
entries.who: Sophomores and juniors at LA County high schools, 16 by the start, living within 25 miles of the Getty Center.

entries.title: DPR Construction Build Up High School Internship
entries.pay: Paid hourly with transportation stipends. Rate not listed.
entries.deadline: 2027 details due early 2027.
entries.who: Rising juniors, rising seniors or May 2027 graduates who can commute to an active DPR jobsite. Family income below 80% of the area median.
entries.oddsNote: A good pick if you like building things more than labs.

entries.title: Get these ready this week
entries.lead: Most of these programs ask for the same few things.
items: Ask one teacher or coach for a recommendation now, before everyone else does.
Request an unofficial transcript from your school.
Make a one-page resume. School projects, clubs and part-time work all count.
If you are under 18, check whether you need a work permit. Some programs ask for one.

action.label: Free application checklist
action.note: Check your application before you send it.

entries.title: These show up on a lot of lists
entries.lead: We checked them too. Here is why they are not above.
items: Lockheed Martin Space High School Internship: open through January 3, 2027, but its program page lists no pay. If you live near a site, ask first.
Bank of America Student Leaders: the 2027 program requires being a rising college sophomore.
Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program: it no longer accepts high school seniors.
Stanford SIMR: pay is limited and needs-based, and students from outside the Bay Area must show they have housing.
Boeing: it says it does not offer internships for high school students.
Google, Apple, Goldman Sachs, Citi and Wells Fargo: we found no public US internship for high schoolers.

verifyNote: Programs change their rules and dates, so confirm on the official page before you apply. The odds labels are our own judgment from the newest public numbers we could find.
